newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Compaq to buy Tandem.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Compaq to buy Tandem.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., taking a major step to expand beyond being the world's largest personal computer maker, said Monday it was acquiring Tandem Computers Inc. for about $3 billion in stock.

Tandem's stock shot up more than 40 percent on the news while Compaq shares slid, both in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Tandem added $5.875 to $20.875 while Compaq lost $2.875 to $104.

Under terms of the agreement, Tandem will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Compaq, which has recently been in merger talks with several companies. Tandem was never mentioned as a possible merger candidate, however, and the deal surprised Wall Street analysts, although most applauded the deal.

Tandem, which is based in Cupertino, Calif., manufactures fault-tolerant, or fail-safe, computer systems for processing on-line transactions. For example, its systems run 90 percent of the world's stock exchanges, including the New York Stock Exchange.
Under the agreement, Compaq will issue some 29 million shares in exchange for all the stock of Tandem. The exchange ratio will be about 0.21 Compaq share for each Tandem share.
Based on Compaq's trading price of $104, the total deal is worth about $3.02 billion, with each Tandem share valued at about $21.84, with Compaq paying a premium of about $1 billion, analysts said.
Houston-based Compaq, which employs about 20,375 people worldwide, had sales of $18.1 billion last year.
Compaq said the deal will fill in the missing gaps in its announced quest to become one of the world's top three computer makers.

"It's a one-stop-shopping, total-enterprise solution," Compaq President Eckhard Pfeiffer said in an interview. "We need to cover the entire spectrum -- software, services and support. That is the road map to being one of the top three global computer companies."
Pfeiffer said the combination will increase the company's total potential market to $650 billion from $200 billion.
He also said the deal will double Compaq's current sales force with Tandem's 4,000 member sales team, add a services and support group and technology to help it move beyond PCs and PC servers.
Tandem's core business is its Himalaya fault-tolerant computers. It also has begun developing Windows NT-based servers.
The companies said the deal will make Compaq/Tandem the No. 1 server supplier in the world. Servers are computers that run and manage corporate networks.

"Tandem is excellent in high-end systems at the enterprise level," said Jay Stevens, a Buckingham Research Group analyst. "Compaq wanted to get up to that level. You can't get to the enterprise level with only PCs and servers. You need proven relationships, software, hardware and Tandem has all of that."
The companies were mum on the financial impact of the deal, except to say that Compaq will see revenue growth.
"We will see very significant revenue growth," Pfeiffer said. But he added that he could not be more specific about any financials related to the merger.
He said Compaq decided to use stock instead of cash for the merger so that it would have a "very clean" merger with a pooling of interests.
Because the transaction will be a pooling of interests, Compaq's board of directors rescinded its previously announced share repurchase program, the company said.

Pfeiffer said Compaq will retain its huge cash pile -- which was $4.7 billion at the end of first quarter -- for other uses, including other deals, should they come up. He declined to comment on Compaq's other reported merger talks.
"It's all rumors and nothing else," Pfeiffer said.

Over the past year, Compaq has been reported to be in talks to acquire Digital Equipment Corp., Gateway 2000 Inc. and Micron Electronics Inc. Shares of all three companies were off Monday as traders said any remaining hopes for a deal with Compaq were quashed by its Tandem merger.
"It's a good match because it will enable them to make servers that no one else can make," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Research analyst.

"They can use the great Tandem technology to make servers as competitive as high-end mainframes and UNIX-based servers," Ries added, referring to the systems that currently dominate the corporate computing market, where high reliability is the most important factor.
The deal is expected to be completed in the third quarter, subject to approval by Tandem shareholders, clearance under anti-trust law and other customary closing conditions.
Merger and acquisition specialists said the transaction probably would encounter little opposition.
Tandem Chairman Tom Perkins has been invited to join the Compaq board.
